<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">On the Semantic and Syntactic Information Encoded in Proto-Tokens for One-Step Text Reconstruction</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Ivan Bondarenko
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">i.bondarenko@g.nsu.ru</span></a>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Egor Palkin
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">e.palkin1@g.nsu.ru</span></a>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Fedor Tikunov
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">f.tikunov@g.nsu.ru</span></a>
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Autoregressive large language models (LLMs) generate text token-by-token, requiring <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> forward passes to produce a sequence of length <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>. Recent work, <em id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Exploring the Latent Capacity of LLMs for One-Step Text Reconstruction</em> (Mezentsev and Oseledets), shows that frozen LLMs can reconstruct hundreds of tokens from only two learned <em id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">proto-tokens</em> in a single forward pass, suggesting a path beyond the autoregressive paradigm.
In this paper, we study what information these proto-tokens encode and how they behave under reconstruction and controlled constraints.
We perform a series of experiments aimed at disentangling semantic and syntactic content in the two proto-tokens, analyzing stability properties of the <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token, and visualizing attention patterns to the <math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token during reconstruction.
Finally, we test two regularization schemes for “imposing” semantic structure on the <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token using teacher embeddings, including an anchor-based loss and a relational distillation objective.
Our results indicate that the <math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>-token tends to capture semantic information more strongly than the <math id="abstract1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token under standard optimization; anchor-based constraints trade off sharply with reconstruction accuracy; and relational distillation can transfer batch-level semantic relations into the proto-token space without sacrificing reconstruction quality, supporting the feasibility of future non-autoregressive seq2seq systems that predict proto-tokens as an intermediate representation.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Autoregressive LLMs generate text in a left-to-right fashion by predicting the next token conditioned on the previously generated context.
This approach has a fundamental computational limitation: generating a sequence of length <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> typically requires <math id="S1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> forward passes of the model.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Non-autoregressive (NAR) text generation aims to reduce this sequential bottleneck by generating multiple tokens (or the whole sequence) in parallel, typically at the cost of additional modeling assumptions, iterative refinement, or distillation from autoregressive teachers.
Recent NAR approaches and analyses provide a broad view of the design space and its trade-offs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work, <em id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Exploring the Latent Capacity of LLMs for One-Step Text Reconstruction</em> (Mezentsev and Oseledets), demonstrates that frozen LLMs can reconstruct hundreds of tokens from only two learned proto-tokens in a single forward pass.
This observation motivates moving beyond the purely autoregressive paradigm.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We view the frozen-LLM plus learned proto-token interface as a complementary perspective on NAR generation: instead of training a fully new NAR model end-to-end, one can (i) keep a strong pretrained decoder frozen, (ii) predict a small set of continuous proto-tokens, and (iii) decode an entire sequence in one pass.
Moreover, our experiments explore explicitly distillation-style constraints (relational distillation) that transfer semantic structure into the proto-token space, connecting this approach to common NAR training recipes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Given such a reconstruction mechanism, a natural question arises: can proto-tokens be used not only for reconstruction, but also for <em id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">controlled</em> sequence continuation?
To answer this question, we must understand what information the proto-tokens (<math id="S1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>) contain and how they behave during generation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we perform the following experimental study of proto-tokens:</p>
<ol id="S1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Semantic content encoded in proto-tokens.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Syntactic content encoded in proto-tokens.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Stability of the <math id="S1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token under optimization and constraints.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Attention visualization to the <math id="S1.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token during reconstruction.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Experiments on imposing semantic structure on the <math id="S1.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token using a teacher vector.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our work is most directly influenced by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mezentsev and Oseledets [1]</a></cite> (“Exploring the Latent Capacity of LLMs for One-Step Text Reconstruction”).
That paper shows that, by feeding two trainable proto-tokens into a frozen LLM and optimizing only their input embeddings, one can reconstruct sequences hundreds of tokens in a single forward pass.
Proto-token embeddings are learned by minimizing a cross-entropy reconstruction objective.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For broader context, we refer to recent work on non-autoregressive generation methods and their training strategies, including distillation-based objectives <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In particular, the input to the frozen LLM can be viewed as a sequence of embeddings where two proto-token embeddings are placed first, followed by a fixed number of repeated <math id="S2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> embeddings:</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=\left[e,\;\underbrace{m,\;m,\;\ldots,\;m}_{T-1}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=\left[e,\;\underbrace{m,\;m,\;\ldots,\;m}_{T-1}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Training optimizes only the proto-token embeddings while the model weights remain frozen. Reconstruction is learned with the standard cross-entropy objective:</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CE}}=-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T}\log p_{\theta}(t_{i}\mid X_{&lt;i})=-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T}\log\left(\frac{\exp(z_{i-1,t_{i}})}{\sum_{c\in V}\exp(z_{i-1,c})}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>CE</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CE}}=-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T}\log p_{\theta}(t_{i}\mid X_{&lt;i})=-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T}\log\left(\frac{\exp(z_{i-1,t_{i}})}{\sum_{c\in V}\exp(z_{i-1,c})}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i-1,\cdot}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">⋅</mo></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i-1,\cdot}</annotation></semantics></math> are the model logits at position <math id="S2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(i-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(i-1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is the vocabulary, and <math id="S2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="S2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th target token.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We extend this direction by analyzing what the two proto-tokens encode.
In particular, we provide evidence that <math id="S2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> contain both semantic and syntactic information, though to different degrees.
These observations suggest the feasibility of a stable non-autoregressive seq2seq architecture in which a separate model predicts proto-tokens from past context, and a frozen LLM decodes them into continuations (e.g., for question answering).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Proto-token optimization for reconstruction</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first describe how we obtain proto-token embeddings for one-step reconstruction.
Let the target token sequence be <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=[t_{1},\ldots,t_{T}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=[t_{1},\ldots,t_{T}]</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> be the hidden size of the frozen causal LLM.
For each example, we optimize two learnable vectors <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e,m\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e,m\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and build a proto-token-only input embedding sequence</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=[e,m,m,\ldots,m]\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=[e,m,m,\ldots,m]\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> is repeated <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(T-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(T-1)</annotation></semantics></math> times.
We feed <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> to the frozen causal LLM with the standard causal attention mask and obtain logits <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times|V|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times|V|}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Following the next-token prediction convention, the logits at position <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(i-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(i-1)</annotation></semantics></math> are used to predict token <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We optimize only <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> using AdamW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> until the reconstruction token accuracy reaches a threshold (e.g., <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9</annotation></semantics></math>) or a maximum number of iterations is reached.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Semantic augmentation experiment</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To probe semantic content in proto-token representations, for each text in a subset of the dataset we generate <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> lexical and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math> semantic augmentations.
For each variant, we optimize proto-token embeddings using the procedure above and then visualize the resulting representations using t-SNE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>.
The core hypothesis is: if proto-tokens encode semantic information, then t-SNE projections of proto-tokens for paraphrases of the same example should cluster together, even when surface form differs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lexical augmentations.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Lexical augmentations are based on introducing typos, including:
(i) random case flips; (ii) frequent orthographic errors; (iii) common keyboard typing errors; and (iv) random deletion/insertion/repetition/swaps of characters.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Semantic augmentations.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Semantic augmentations are paraphrases generated by an LLM (Qwen3-4B).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Imposing semantic structure on the <math id="S3.SS3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because the semantic clustering for the <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token was weak in the experiment above, we hypothesize that non-autoregressive optimization admits many good solutions for <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(e,m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(e,m)</annotation></semantics></math>, and random initialization can lead to <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> vectors that do not preserve semantic relations across examples.
This motivates adding additional constraints to encourage semantic structure.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Terminology.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Throughout the paper we use the terms <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">proto-tokens</em>, <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic"><math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token</em>, and <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic"><math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>-token</em> consistently.
We refer to the decoding setting studied here as <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">one-step reconstruction</em> (not “one-step generation”).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate two regularization schemes:</p>
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Anchor loss.</span> We add a term that encourages <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> to stay close to a teacher embedding <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> (obtained from Qwen3-Embedding-8B). We also initialize <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{anchor}}=1-\cos(e_{i},t_{i})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>anchor</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{anchor}}=1-\cos(e_{i},t_{i}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We combine the reconstruction loss with optional regularizers:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CE}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{anchor}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{anchor}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rel}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>CE</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>anchor</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>anchor</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>rel</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>rel</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CE}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{anchor}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{anchor}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rel}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The anchor term is weighted by a separate hyperparameter in the global loss.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Relational distillation.</span> We penalize mismatch between pairwise similarity matrices (using MSE/Huber) computed from teacher embeddings <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and student embeddings <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> within a batch:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{1}{B(B-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}\ell\left(S^{(E)}_{ij},\,S^{(T)}_{ij}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>rel</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{1}{B(B-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}\ell\left(S^{(E)}_{ij},\,S^{(T)}_{ij}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is the batch size, <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{(T)}_{ij}=\cos(t_{i},t_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{(T)}_{ij}=\cos(t_{i},t_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> (teacher) and <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{(E)}_{ij}=\cos(e_{i},e_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{(E)}_{ij}=\cos(e_{i},e_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> (student), and <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(a,b)=(a-b)^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(a,b)=(a-b)^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (MSE) or <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(a,b)=\mathrm{Huber}(a-b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Huber</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(a,b)=\mathrm{Huber}(a-b)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Syntactic experiment</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To probe syntactic content, we generate seven classes of sentences using an LLM and context-free grammars:
(1) simple, (2) complex, (3) simple interrogative, (4) complex interrogative, (5) simple imperative, (6) complex imperative, and (7) one-clause (single-member) sentences.
We then test whether t-SNE projections of proto-token representations cluster by syntactic class.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Attention visualization</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We also visualize attention weights to the <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token across layers and heads.
Because of causal masking, the <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token does not attend to later tokens; thus we focus on how other positions attend <em id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">to</em> <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> during reconstruction.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments and Results</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Attention visualization to the <math id="S4.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We visualize attention weights <em id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">to</em> the <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token during one-step reconstruction.
Because of causal masking, the <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token does not attend to later positions; thus we focus on how other tokens attend to <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> across layers and heads.
For each example, we first obtain proto-tokens that reconstruct the target sequence well, then run the frozen model forward and extract attention maps.</p>
</div>

</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Robustness to additive noise in proto-tokens</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We study how additive noise affects reconstruction quality when perturbing the optimized proto-token embeddings, focusing on the stability of the reconstruction process under embedding-level disturbances.
Given optimized proto-tokens <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(e,m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(e,m)</annotation></semantics></math> for a text example, we add noise to the <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token and measure reconstruction token accuracy as a function of noise intensity and distribution.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Noise distributions.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider four types of noise:</p>
<ol id="S4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Gaussian: <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Uniform: <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{U}(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{U}(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Exponential: <math id="S4.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\sim\mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\sim\mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sinusoidal: <math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon=\sin(\omega i+\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon=\sin(\omega i+\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> (structured perturbation).</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Normalization.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We scale the noise to control its magnitude relative to the original embedding norm:</p>
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\varepsilon}=\frac{\varepsilon}{\lVert\varepsilon\rVert_{2}}\cdot\alpha\cdot\lVert e\rVert_{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ε</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>ε</mi><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0.055em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mi>e</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\varepsilon}=\frac{\varepsilon}{\lVert\varepsilon\rVert_{2}}\cdot\alpha\cdot\lVert e\rVert_{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in\{0.0,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in\{0.0,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0\}</annotation></semantics></math> controls intensity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18301v1/noiseeffect.png" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/268;" width="333" height="268" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S4.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Reconstruction accuracy as a function of noise intensity <math id="S4.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> for different noise types.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As expected, reconstruction quality degrades as the noise level increases; different noise distributions exhibit similar trends in our setup.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Models and data</h3>

<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Models.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use Llama-3.2-1B to obtain optimized proto-token embeddings, Qwen3-4B to generate paraphrases, and Qwen3-Embedding-8B to produce teacher vectors.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Data.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the semantic experiment, we use the databricks-dolly-15k dataset of instruction-following pairs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>.
We generate paraphrases via Qwen3-4B and typo-based variants via the <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">augmentex</span> library <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>.
For semantic-imposition and attention-visualization experiments, we also use Dolly.
For the syntactic experiment, we use fully synthetic data generated by Qwen3-4B and context-free grammars; the grammar vocabulary is built from the 500 most frequent words in the Brown corpus categories “news”, “editorial”, “learned”, and “reviews” <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, with POS tags assigned via WordNet matches <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimization details.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Proto-token embeddings are optimized with AdamW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> using learning rate <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=\beta_{2}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=\beta_{2}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math>, and weight decay <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math>.
We use <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=\beta_{2}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=\beta_{2}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math> following preliminary tuning.
We optimize each example until token accuracy reaches <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9</annotation></semantics></math> or for at most 2000 iterations.
Embeddings are initialized from a standard normal distribution unless otherwise stated.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Semantic content: <math id="S4.SS4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="S4.SS4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">From t-SNE visualizations, we observe that the <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>-token embeddings exhibit stronger semantic clustering than <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> under standard optimization.
This suggests that <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> carries more semantic information about the sentence content, while <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> may encode other factors (or be less identifiable across solutions).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18301v1/fig_tsne_e.png" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:310/241;" width="310" height="241" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">t-SNE visualization of optimized <math id="S4.F5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token embeddings for original, lexical, and semantic augmentations.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18301v1/fig_tsne_m.png" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:310/241;" width="310" height="241" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">t-SNE visualization of optimized <math id="S4.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>-token embeddings for original, lexical, and semantic augmentations.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Imposing semantics on <math id="S4.SS5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Anchor loss.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With a small anchor weight (e.g., <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.02</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.02</annotation></semantics></math> multiplying the anchor term in the global loss), reconstruction can remain mostly successful.
However, the final cosine similarity between <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> and the teacher vector remains close to zero in our runs.
Increasing the anchor weight (e.g., to <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>) substantially degrades reconstruction accuracy while increasing the final similarity.
Overall, these results do not support the hypothesis that <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> can be forced to match an off-the-shelf sentence embedding while preserving reconstruction quality.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18301v1/fig_anchor_acc_small.png" id="S4.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:310/232;" width="310" height="232" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S4.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Reconstruction token accuracy vs. target length under anchor regularization with a small weight.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18301v1/fig_anchor_cos_small.png" id="S4.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:310/248;" width="310" height="248" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="S4.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cosine similarity between <math id="S4.F8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> and the teacher embedding over optimization steps (anchor).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18301v1/fig_anchor_cos_large.png" id="S4.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:310/243;" width="310" height="243" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S4.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cosine similarity between <math id="S4.F9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> and the teacher embedding over optimization steps for a larger anchor weight.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18301v1/fig_anchor_acc_large.png" id="S4.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:310/232;" width="310" height="232" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="S4.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Token accuracy vs. target length for a larger anchor weight, showing degraded reconstruction.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relational distillation.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using relational distillation, we find that even without constraints there is weak semantic structure in <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-tokens, but it becomes more apparent when using a shared <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>-token.
Importantly, adding the relational constraint preserves the ability to reconstruct text accurately while significantly improving correlation between teacher and student similarity matrices across batches (batch size 6).
This indicates that relational distillation can transfer semantic relations into the proto-token space without sacrificing reconstruction.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F11" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

</figure></div></div>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.6 </span>Syntactic content and attention patterns</h3>

<div id="S4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our syntactic clustering and attention analyses suggest that proto-tokens also encode information correlated with syntactic structure.
These observations support the working hypothesis that, if <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> is more semantically aligned, then <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> may carry more syntactic information; we leave a detailed quantitative study as future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Discussion and Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We studied proto-tokens used for one-step reconstruction with frozen LLMs and investigated what information they encode.
Our experiments indicate that:</p>
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under unconstrained optimization, the <math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>-token tends to capture semantic information more strongly than the <math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Anchor-based regularization that forces <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> toward a teacher sentence embedding introduces a sharp trade-off: stronger anchoring improves similarity but quickly harms reconstruction accuracy, and weak anchoring does not reliably align <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> with the teacher space.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Relational distillation is a more promising alternative: it transfers batch-level semantic relations into the proto-token space while preserving high reconstruction performance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Proto-tokens appear to encode syntactic information as well, and attention patterns suggest that the model actively uses the <math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>-token during decoding.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These findings support the feasibility of a non-autoregressive seq2seq pipeline in which a lightweight predictor maps context to proto-tokens, and a frozen LLM decodes them into text.
Future work includes (i) building an explicit proto-token predictor for controlled generation, (ii) quantifying syntactic vs. semantic disentanglement, and (iii) improving identifiability and stability of proto-token representations across optimization runs.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Training and Optimization Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Prototype Token Initialization</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Prototype token embeddings were initialized from a standard normal distribution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Optimization</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Embeddings were optimized using the AdamW optimizer with the following hyperparameters:</p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Learning rate: 0.01</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{2}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{2}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Weight decay: 0.01</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All other parameters were kept at default values.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Semantic Augmentation Experiment</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Lexical augmentations</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Character-level lexical augmentation was performed using the <span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">augmentex</span> library with the following configuration:</p>
<ul id="A2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Character modification probability: 0.3</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Minimum number of augmentations per sentence: 1</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Maximum number of augmentations per sentence: 5</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Maximum character repetition factor: 3</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Keyboard layout for typo simulation: PC</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Semantic augmentations</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Semantic paraphrases were generated using the Qwen3-4B language model. The decoding parameters were:</p>
<ul id="A2.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Temperature: 0.7</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Top-p: 0.9</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Syntactic Augmentation Experiment</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To probe syntactic content, we generated seven sentence classes using an LLM and context-free grammars.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Lexical Resources for CFG Generation</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Lexical resources for CFG generation were derived as follows:</p>
<ol id="A3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The 500 most frequent words were extracted from the Brown corpus, restricted to the categories <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">news</span>, <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">editorial</span>, <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">learned</span>, and <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">reviews</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each word was assigned a part of speech using WordNet synsets and POS tagging to ensure grammatical correctness.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>LLM Generation</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For syntactic sentence generation via the LLM, we used Qwen3-4B. The decoding parameters were:</p>
<ul id="A3.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A3.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Temperature: 0.7</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Top-p: 0.9</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
